verdicts.note: Refers to herself among 'the girls'; female subject throughout.
On a design & technology course; quote is A-levels but D&T enrolment is clear.
Mixed design group with few girls implies mixed-sex school; reasonable at medium.
Done 2 years, placement before final year = Part B/Year 2.
Quote is about girls in general and course grades, not her own maths/science ability at school; does not support the construct.
Didn't know what engineering was, did no research; strong support.
Parents (OT, computer programmer) not in design/eng industry = disagree.
Values degree though uncommitted to profession; quote generic but consistent with agree.
Careers advice 'absolutely useless'; no encouragement = strongly disagree.
Mother actively researched/looked at courses for her; supports agree (not strongly).
Quote is about her lack of regret, not about whether anyone discouraged her; does not evidence the construct (family-supportive exchange would have been the right quote).
Secured placement, met manager; yes.
'nice to do a proper job' is mild; supports agree, not Strongly agree (experience not emphasised among her reasons).
'I want to stall for a year' / 'break in the middle' strongly supports break from education.
Interesting to see what the workplace is like = wants idea of industry.
Placement year 'telling'; will help decide future direction.
Hopes to get ideas for final project from placement.
Repeats institutional line ('we get told') about helping the final year, not grade improvement, and immediately hedges ('I hope so, I don't know'); does not evidence her own agreement.
'Mostly the fact that I'll be able to buy a car' makes money a key draw; agree defensible.
Prefers managerial/office over design; project management is nearest within-field option.
Explicitly 'quite like to be sort of managerial'.
She explicitly said 'I wasn't trying to think about location... I'd go anywhere' (twice); proximity to friends is a bonus, not a decision factor, so location was not important.
Development opportunities impressed her and drove acceptance; important.
'Yes I do' to liking group work; satisfied despite organisational cons.
Strongly positive about personal tutor's genuine interest; very satisfied.
'I like the making things' = satisfied with practical work.
Coursework amount 'phenomenal'/'nightmare' = dissatisfied with quantity.
Sociable, group-heavy course; supports developing interpersonal skills, though somewhat inferential.
'I don't regret it at all... good for me' = pleased with choice.
Interviewer supplied the word 'competitive' and she merely echoed it; also framed around industry/culture not students. Interviewer-planted -> reject.
As female minority risks being 'shouted down'/needs to be strong-minded; implies males more dominant/confident.
Technicians 'more inclined to help the girls' = female students get more help.
